entities.name: knaithe
entities.description: Chinese-speaking threat actor who orchestrated an AI-enabled autonomous hacking campaign, combining autonomous AI-driven enumeration with manual exploitation achieving confirmed impact. Based in Zhuhai, China, and self-described as an opportunistic exploit operator and binary security researcher.
entities.evidence_quote: The actor, operating under the aliases knaithe and KnYuan, leveraged DeepSeek, via the Hermes Agent framework, as their autonomous offensive operator.

entities.name: DeepSeek
entities.description: Large language model used by the actor as their autonomous offensive operator/reasoning engine, accessed via the Hermes Agent framework, chosen for its lack of built-in safety layer.
entities.evidence_quote: leveraged DeepSeek, via the Hermes Agent framework, as their autonomous offensive operator

entities.name: Hermes Agent
entities.description: Open-source AI agent orchestration framework used by the actor to provide terminal access, Telegram-based command and control, and a skills system, with DeepSeek as its reasoning engine.
entities.evidence_quote: Hermes Agent provided orchestration (terminal access, Telegram-based command and control, and the skills system) while DeepSeek served as the reasoning engine

entities.name: Qwen
entities.description: Large language model configured by the actor alongside GLM, Kimi, and MiniMax, consistent with evaluating Chinese-market AI models; Qwen Code saw minimal usage (two sessions).
entities.evidence_quote: the actor configured multiple large language models (LLMs) (Qwen, GLM, Kimi, MiniMax)

entities.name: GLM
entities.description: Large language model configured by the actor as part of evaluating multiple AI platforms.
entities.evidence_quote: the actor configured multiple large language models (LLMs) (Qwen, GLM, Kimi, MiniMax)

entities.name: Kimi
entities.description: Large language model configured by the actor as part of evaluating multiple AI platforms.
entities.evidence_quote: the actor configured multiple large language models (LLMs) (Qwen, GLM, Kimi, MiniMax)

entities.name: MiniMax
entities.description: Large language model configured by the actor as part of evaluating multiple AI platforms.
entities.evidence_quote: the actor configured multiple large language models (LLMs) (Qwen, GLM, Kimi, MiniMax)

entities.name: Claude Code
entities.description: Western AI coding tool used in limited capacity by the actor for connectivity testing and proxy validation, routed through a third-party proxy to reduce traceability; anti-attribution settings enabled.
entities.evidence_quote: Claude Code for connectivity testing and proxy validation

entities.name: Codex
entities.description: Western AI coding tool showing signs of usage on exploit development directories; actor marked directories as trusted granting full access; response storage disabled to limit forensic evidence; account later flagged/disabled by OpenAI's provider-side safety systems.
entities.evidence_quote: There were also signs of usage of Codex on exploit development directories.

entities.name: FofaMap-Platinum-Full-Expert MCP server
entities.description: Open-source Model Context Protocol (MCP) server integrated by the actor, exposing FOFA asset search, Nuclei scan generation, and a DeepSeek-powered natural-language-to-FOFA query translator.
entities.evidence_quote: The actor also integrated the open-source FofaMap-Platinum-Full-Expert Model Context Protocol (MCP) server

entities.name: FOFA
entities.description: Internet asset search engine used by the actor (via custom fofoapi.py script and MCP integration) to enumerate targets and their vulnerabilities.
entities.evidence_quote: Independently enumerating targets and their vulnerabilities using FOFA

entities.name: 1DayNews
entities.description: Automated vulnerability intelligence pipeline maintained by the actor on GitHub that aggregates RCE disclosures from 17 sources, uses DeepSeek to filter for exploitability, and distributes alerts via Telegram.
entities.evidence_quote: their maintenance of 1DayNews, an automated vulnerability intelligence pipeline

entities.name: Telegram
entities.description: Messaging platform used by the actor to orchestrate the Hermes Agent operator and to distribute vulnerability alerts from 1DayNews.
entities.evidence_quote: They orchestrated this operator via Telegram for the following activities

entities.name: code.newcli.com proxy
entities.description: Third-party proxy service used by the actor to route Claude Code and Codex traffic to reduce traceability.
entities.evidence_quote: They routed the two Western tools, Claude Code and Codex, through a third-party proxy service (code.newcli[.]com) to reduce traceability.

entities.name: Actor home directory file server
entities.description: HTTP file server started by the Hermes Agent from the actor's home directory (/home/worker), which inadvertently exposed the actor's entire operational workspace including tool configurations, API keys, exploit scripts, target lists, and session logs.
entities.evidence_quote: Hermes Agent, responding to a Telegram command, started an HTTP file server (python3 -m http.server 8888) from the actor's home directory (/home/worker)

entities.name: CVE-2026-33017
entities.description: Vulnerability in Langflow exploited autonomously by the actor's Hermes Agent/DeepSeek; exploitation attempt failed because auto_login was disabled.
entities.evidence_quote: DeepSeek identified a Langflow vulnerability (CVE-2026-33017, CVSS 9.8) and autonomously attempted exploitation

entities.name: CVE-2026-21858
entities.description: n8n arbitrary file read vulnerability, CVSS 10.0, patched in 1.121.0, chained with CVE-2025-68613 by the actor's autonomous DeepSeek-driven exploitation attempts against n8n; failed due to authentication requirements.
entities.evidence_quote: CVE-2026-21858 (arbitrary file read, CVSS 10.0)

entities.name: CVE-2025-68613
entities.description: n8n sandbox bypass to remote code execution vulnerability, CVSS 9.9, patched in 1.120.4, chained with CVE-2026-21858 in the actor's autonomous exploitation attempts against n8n.
entities.evidence_quote: CVE-2025-68613 (sandbox bypass to remote code execution (RCE), CVSS 9.9)

entities.name: CVE-2026-3055
entities.description: Citrix NetScaler ADC & Gateway out-of-bounds memory read vulnerability manually exploited by the actor, resulting in data exfiltration from three organizations, including a persistently targeted Malaysian government entity.
entities.evidence_quote: Data exfiltration from three organizations via a Citrix NetScaler vulnerability (CVE-2026-3055)

entities.name: CVE-2026-39987
entities.description: Marimo Notebook vulnerability manually exploited by the actor, resulting in confirmed command execution on 11 instances.
entities.evidence_quote: Command execution on 11 Marimo notebook instances (CVE-2026-39987)

entities.name: CVE-2026-34486
entities.description: Apache Tomcat Java deserialization vulnerability manually exploited by the actor via reverse shell attempts against nine servers.
entities.evidence_quote: Java deserialization reverse shell attempts against nine Apache Tomcat servers (CVE-2026-34486)

entities.name: CVE-2026-33824
entities.description: Windows IKE Extensions (IKE VPN) vulnerability manually exploited by the actor via reverse shell callbacks targeting three IKE VPN endpoints.
entities.evidence_quote: Reverse shell callbacks targeting three IKE VPN endpoints (CVE-2026-33824)

entities.name: CVE-2026-0300
entities.description: Buffer overflow vulnerability in PAN-OS User-ID Authentication Portal (Captive Portal); actor cloned a public non-functional PoC repository but did not achieve execution.
entities.evidence_quote: The actor cloned a public repository (qassam-315/PAN-OS-User-ID-Buffer-Overflow-PoC) for CVE-2026-0300, a buffer overflow vulnerability in the PAN-OS User-ID Authentication Portal

entities.name: Autonomous vulnerability enumeration and exploitation via AI agent
entities.description: The actor used the Hermes Agent/DeepSeek to autonomously enumerate targets via FOFA, search for PoCs on GitHub, prioritize vulnerabilities, and attempt exploitation without human intervention.
entities.evidence_quote: Their Hermes Agent autonomously conducted searches for known critical-severity Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs).

entities.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
entities.description: The actor exploited public-facing applications (Langflow, n8n, Citrix NetScaler, Marimo, Tomcat, IKE VPN, PAN-OS) using known CVEs.
entities.evidence_quote: targeted infrastructure using seven vulnerabilities, combining autonomous AI-driven enumeration with manual exploitation

entities.name: Data exfiltration via memory read vulnerability
entities.description: The actor exploited Citrix NetScaler's out-of-bounds memory read to exfiltrate memory data and search for authentication cookies, indicating session hijacking intent.
entities.evidence_quote: The actor searched the exfiltrated data for NetScaler authentication cookies (NSC_AAAC=), indicating session hijacking intent.

entities.name: Unauthenticated WebSocket exploitation
entities.description: Custom-created skill within Hermes Agent for exploiting unauthenticated WebSocket services.
entities.evidence_quote: web-terminal-exploitation: unauthenticated WebSocket exploitation, custom-created

entities.name: LLM jailbreaking (godmode)
entities.description: A framework-bundled red-teaming skill named godmode used to jailbreak the LLM and remove safety restrictions for offensive use.
entities.evidence_quote: godmode: LLM jailbreaking, framework-bundled

entities.name: Reverse shell deployment
entities.description: The actor attempted reverse shell callbacks/attempts against Apache Tomcat and IKE VPN endpoints.
entities.evidence_quote: Reverse shell callbacks targeting three IKE VPN endpoints (CVE-2026-33824)

entities.name: AI-enabled autonomous hacking campaign by knaithe/KnYuan
entities.description: Campaign combining autonomous AI-driven vulnerability enumeration and exploitation (via DeepSeek/Hermes Agent) with manual exploitation techniques, targeting infrastructure across three countries using seven vulnerabilities.

properties.objective: Opportunistic exploitation of internet-facing infrastructure, data exfiltration, and establishing autonomous AI offensive capability

entities.evidence_quote: Unit 42 identified an AI-enabled autonomous hacking campaign carried out by a Chinese-speaking threat actor.

entities.name: China
entities.description: Country where the threat actor is based (Zhuhai) and where the autonomous AI campaigns targeted domestic infrastructure indiscriminately.
entities.evidence_quote: The Chinese-speaking actor is based in Zhuhai, China

entities.name: Malaysia
entities.description: Country whose government entity was persistently and manually targeted by the actor over multiple days with refined exploitation and proxy anonymization.
entities.evidence_quote: The actor persistently targeted a government entity in Malaysia and they exploited it over multiple days

entities.name: Government entity in Malaysia
entities.description: Malaysian government victim organization targeted persistently via Citrix NetScaler exploitation with data exfiltration and session hijacking intent.
entities.evidence_quote: The actor persistently targeted a government entity in Malaysia and they exploited it over multiple days with memory grooming parameters and maximum read attempts.

entities.name: Qwen Code

entities.evidence_quote: Qwen Code: There was minimal usage by the actor, including two sessions total.
